item.title: Walk on Multiscale Media: Compiling Editable and Composable Transport Medium Prefabs for Monte Carlo PDE Solvers
item.description: arXiv:2610.35952v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Monte Carlo PDE solvers enable mesh-free pointwise queries, but repeatedly traversing heterogeneous media is costly, particularly in scenes with reusable or dynamically changing materials. We introduce Walk on Multiscale Media (WoMM), which compiles fine-scale transport into reusable, editable and composable transport prefabs. A probabilistic interpretation of multiscale finite-element bases and condensed operators yields coarse transitions retaining fine-scale material effects. Each prefab combines port-level operators, entrance-dependent exit distributions, and Poisson-marked trajectory records, enabling incremental updates for overlapping absorption fields, gradient-field steering through path reweighting and transient diffusion. Integrated with conventional Walk-on-Spheres in a hybrid continuous--discrete solver, these prefabs accelerate repeated pointwise PDE queries and support interactive material edits without repeatedly solving the fine-scale problem.
item.dc:creator: Yunfeng Liao, Xiucheng Li

item.title: Evaluation of upper-scale mechanical parameters of particulate aluminum-based nanocomposites from molecular simulations
item.description: arXiv:2610.36005v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper focuses on the numerical and analytical determination of the mechanical parameters of aluminum-matrix nanocomposites using atomistic-scale simulations within a multiscale modeling framework. Molecular statics simulations were employed to evaluate the tensile and compressive behavior of Al based composites reinforced with nanosized alumina particles. Two classes of atomistic models were investigated. First, a unit-cell model containing a single Al2O3 monocrystal embedded in an aluminum matrix was used to examine the influence of the volume fraction of the ceramic inclusion on the effective mechanical properties. Second, a polycrystalline RVE model comprising an alumina particle was analyzed to assess the effect of the number of Al grains on effective properties. For each case, the mechanical response was characterized by stress-strain curves, enabling the identification of upper-scale material parameters associated with the elastic regime (bulk, shear and Young's modulus) and the damage stage (ultimate strength, ultimate strain, and failure strain). The isotropized elastic constants evaluated from molecular simulations were compared with classical Voigt-Reuss-Hill bounds to assess their applicability in the elastic regime. Finally, atomistic-scale simulation outputs provided insight into the dominant deformation/damage mechanisms (brittle versus ductile) and fracture modes (transgranular versus intergranular).
item.dc:creator: Bartosz Bucholc, Marcin Ma\'zdziarz, Szymon Nosewicz

item.title: Efficient regime boundary detection in discontinuous simulation models
item.description: arXiv:2610.36092v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Many computational models exhibit multiple operating regimes separated by abrupt or non-smooth transitions as the input parameters vary. Such regime transitions complicate the construction of global parametric reduced-order models, often necessitating large training datasets to capture the distinct system behaviors. Accurate regime boundary detection instead enables localized modeling strategies by partitioning the parameter space into regions of qualitatively distinct behavior. In many cases, regime switching corresponds to the excursion set of a simulator output. When such a quantity is discontinuous or non-smooth, regression-based algorithms for level set estimation can struggle to correctly approximate the boundary. In this work, we show that solving a resulting binary classification problem can improve sample efficiency and we further propose a novel adaptive sampling strategy for support vector machines. Unlike uncertainty-based sampling schemes, the proposed approach uses a continuous search space and efficiently explores the currently estimated boundary in its tangential directions by gradient-based dynamic sampling. Because the decision function admits analytical gradients, this exploration incurs negligible computational overhead relative to the underlying model evaluations. Then, a space-filling subset of the generated samples is selected as the next batch to be queried. We demonstrate improved sample efficiency compared to existing active learning algorithms on analytical and numerical examples. The proposed method provides a sample-efficient framework for regime boundary detection in a broad class of discontinuous simulation-driven problems.
item.dc:creator: Federico Betti, Eleni Chatzi, Paolo Tiso

item.title: QMOMKit: A C++ library for quadrature-based moment methods
item.description: arXiv:2610.36189v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: QMOMKit is an open-source C++ library for the phase-space evolution of population balance equations with quadrature-based moment methods. The present version implements the quadrature method of moments (QMOM) and the conditional quadrature method of moments (CQMOM). QMOMKit is designed to be independent of any particular application and can be used either as a standalone solver for spatially homogeneous population models or as a local phase-space solver coupled to a host application. It handles the numerical aspects of the evolution of a population in phase space, including quadrature reconstruction, advection of the quadrature abscissas, and changes to the population through moment sources and phase-space boundary contributions. The number of quadrature nodes is adapted to what the supplied moments support, subject to prescribed bounds of the phase-space coordinates, and the CQMOM implementation supports an arbitrary number of phase-space dimensions as well as any conditioning order. The principal numerical algorithms of QMOMKit are verified against analytical and manufactured solutions. Standalone spatially homogeneous applications, ranging from aerosol evaporation to particle dynamics and fragmentation, are compared with Monte Carlo solutions of the same population models, while coupling examples with OpenFOAM and deal.II demonstrate how QMOMKit can be embedded in finite-volume and discontinuous-Galerkin simulation frameworks. Together, these capabilities provide a tested and reusable foundation for a wide range of population-balance problems, and a basis for extending QMOMKit to other quadrature-based moment methods.
item.dc:creator: Fabian Denner, Bruna Campos, Bruno Blais

item.title: Fast diagonalization for matrix-free inversion of the nodal even-parity operator in hybrid finite element SPN transport
item.description: arXiv:2610.36716v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The hybrid finite element method stores a dense inverse of the nodal even-parity operator for every node and energy group, and that storage limits the spatial and angular expansion orders, more tightly still on a GPU, whose memory is smaller than that of a host. This work introduces fast diagonalization for the nodal even-parity operator of the hybrid finite element SPN method: the stored dense inverse is replaced by the eigendecompositions of a planar, an axial and an angular factor, and the inverse is applied without being formed explicitly. Every even-parity moment of the SPN equations obeys an equation of the same diffusion form, with no mixed derivatives, so the angular coupling is the same in every spatial direction. On a node extruded along the axis, the operator is then an exact Kronecker sum of the three factors. The factorization merely recasts the computation, so the discretization and the solution are unchanged, and the nodes are not required to be identical to one another. The method is implemented for CPU and GPU hardware and compared with the dense inverse within one solver. On a pressurized water reactor core in SP3, the two paths agree to within round-off error, the storage falls from 3.76 GB to 821 kB, and the calculation is 4.15 times faster. On a 33-group fast reactor core, the dense inverse would occupy 24.9 GB and the dense path would need more memory than both the device and the host provide, whereas the factors occupy only 1.26 MB, so the solution can be obtained. The factorization thus reduces the storage of the nodal inverse by more than three orders of magnitude and brings multigroup core calculations at their required spatial expansion orders within the memory of a single GPU.
item.dc:creator: Kyung Min Kim, Yeon Sang Jung

item.title: DSMC Study of Hypersonic Boundary-Layer Unsteadiness Using Data-Driven Analysis
item.description: arXiv:2610.36248v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The prediction of transition remains challenging because the receptivity amplitude is usually prescribed rather than measured. This work uses Direct Simulation Monte Carlo (DSMC) to study an unforced Mach 6 nitrogen boundary layer over a 120 mm flat plate, with no imposed inlet wave, wall signal, modal shape, or disturbance spectrum. The retained unsteady field is the intrinsic finite-particle stochastic fluctuation field carried by the DSMC representation. Changing the DSMC particle count provides an independent numerical control parameter that sets a predictable finite-particle noise floor while preserving the time-averaged boundary-layer flow. Dynamic Mode Decomposition (DMD) is then applied to unforced DSMC snapshots. The DMD eigenvalues and spatial modes estimate the quantities that appear in the LST normal-mode description, including frequency, temporal growth or decay, wavenumber, wavelength, phase speed, mode location, and amplification envelope. LST is used after extraction to test whether the data-derived structures occupy the expected second-mode band. The results show that DSMC data can connect a measured finite-particle stochastic disturbance level to second-mode instability dynamics without imposed disturbance spectra.
item.dc:creator: Mert Senkardesler, Irmak T. Karpuzcu, Deborah A. Levin, Vassilis Theofilis

item.title: Reduced magnetohydrodynamics with electron inertia in pseudodipole coordinates
item.description: arXiv:2610.36262v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the altitude-dependent structuring of field-aligned currents by driven Alfv\'en waves in an expanding auroral flux tube. The model uses the reduced magnetohydrodynamics (RMHD) long-thin ordering assumptions along with electron inertia. We derive a magnetic tension operator consistent with energy conservation in the expanding geometry. We compare uniform density with a prescribed profile containing a dense ionospheric end and a low-density upper region. The simulations produce localized current concentrations near the lower boundary and filamentary structures at greater heights. Broad structures remain visible in the magnetic and velocity stream functions while their perpendicular derivatives reveal finer magnetic field, velocity, and current structure. With the nonuniform density profile, the run with additional upper boundary reflection shows finer current structure and greater numerical dissipation. Spectral diagnostics show forward nonlinear energy transfer and altitude-dependent power-law-like intervals without a broad constant-flux range. The narrowest current concentrations span only a few grid cells, so their physical widths remain unresolved.
item.dc:creator: Khilav Majmudar, Robert L. Lysak

item.title: Effective Noise Thresholds for Reliable Quantum Approximation Optimisation Algorithm under Noisy Environment
item.description: arXiv:2610.36597v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Variational quantum algorithms are leading candidates for practical utilisation on noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) processors, but accumulating noise bounds the usefulness of circuit depths. For the quantum approximate optimisation algorithm (QAOA), this trade-off has mostly been addressed by searching for the best depth for a given device. In this work, we consider the inverse question: how much noise each depth can tolerate. Using GPU-accelerated noisy QAOA simulations for MaxCut on three graph families with 6 to 18 vertices, depths up to 10 and three noise channels, we fit the approximation ratios with a generalised logistic surface. We propose the effective noise threshold as the inflection boundary of the logistic surfaces, a noise boundary separating reliable and unreliable QAOA approximation regimes. In general, the threshold decreases as depth rises, indicating that deeper circuits demand for stricter noise requirement for reliable approximation. Its best and worst values over depth divide the noise axis into three regions: every depth remains effective, depth must be chosen with care, or no depth induces effective optimisation. Assessing on the ibm_marrakesh processor, although modelled gate errors understate factual noise, the threshold modeling remains beneficial in informing qualitative depth-dependence structure and identifying dominating noise channel in noisy QAOA.
item.dc:creator: Yozef Tjandra, Hendrik Santoso Sugiarto, Celine Vania Setiadi, Joanna Gracia Tan, Andriyan Bayu Suksmono

item.title: Local Metrics for Exact Streaming on Curvilinear Lattices: A Curvilinear D3Q27 Cumulant Lattice-Boltzmann Method
item.description: arXiv:2610.36971v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A three-dimensional curvilinear lattice-Boltzmann method is introduced for simulations on smoothly deformed grids while retaining exact one-to-one streaming on a uniform computational lattice. The coordinate transformation is represented locally through a metric-Gaussian equilibrium and a Christoffel-connection source in moment space. A dynamically reconstructed homogeneous-state perturbation streaming procedure preserves homogeneous physical states on warped meshes without interpolation in the advection step. The method is implemented on a D3Q27 lattice with a cumulant collision operator, while the geometric construction remains compatible with other local collision models. The formulation is assessed using two sets of tests. First, static non-orthogonal warped-cube cases validate the bulk curvilinear solver through a convected helical shear wave, the Taylor--Green vortex, and Arnold--Beltrami--Childress flow. These tests verify viscous decay, clean freestream preservation, vortex-breakdown dynamics, and the nonlinear inertial--pressure balance induced by geometric acceleration. Second, wall-bounded and moving-boundary demonstrations assess the boundary-compatible extension through warped plane Poiseuille flow, arbitrary Lagrangian--Eulerian (ALE) peristaltic pumping, and a two-way fluid--structure interaction (FSI) case with added-mass frequency shift. The results show that the proposed curvilinear LBM avoids interpolation-based transport, reduces geometry-locked numerical modes, preserves global mass and momentum to round-off accuracy in the tested warped periodic cases, and extends to wall-bounded ALE/FSI configurations with conservative treatment of mass and physically consistent momentum exchange.
item.dc:creator: Maher Sawaf, Jonas Latt, Nikolaus A. Adams, Mostafa S. Shadloo

item.title: Spin-Orbit-Torque-Driven Recurrent Motion of Synthetic Antiferromagnetic Skyrmions for Magnetic Clocking
item.description: arXiv:2610.37014v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Magnetic skyrmions in synthetic antiferromagnets have emerged as attractive information carriers for spintronic technologies due to their compensated topology, which mitigates the skyrmion Hall effect and facilitates reliable current-driven transport. Here we present a frequency-tunable magnetic clocking concept based on the recurring translational motion of SAF skyrmions and define the material conditions needed to realize it in a Pt/Co/Ru/Pt/Co multilayer. Using micromagnetic simulations, we investigate the combined effects of interfacial Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction and interlayer Ruderman-Kittel-Kasuya-Yosida exchange coupling, delineating the parameter space in which coupled N\'eel-type skyrmions with opposite topological charges form a stable, topologically compensated pair. Under spin-orbit torque excitation, the SAF skyrmions exhibit resilient longitudinal transport with minimal transverse deflection using periodic boundary conditions. Periodic boundary conditions serve as an idealized model for closed-loop racetrack geometries, facilitating the study of continuous transport cycles and long-range steady-state dynamics. The oscillation frequency is readily modified by the applied current density and material characteristics, offering a pathway to field-free nanoscale timing components. Moreover, the threshold-activated initiation of recurrent transport mimics tonic-spiking behavior, indicating possible use in neuromorphic signal generation. This work establishes SAF skyrmions as versatile building elements for future spintronic functional devices by integrating topological protection, controllable transport, and cyclic dynamics.
item.dc:creator: Sayan Mathur, Payal Bhattacharjee, Saswati Barman, Anjan Barman

item.title: DSMC Study on Unsteadiness of Supersonic Flow Over a Cylinder
item.description: arXiv:2610.37048v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Unsteady flow over a 30 $\mu$m diameter cylinder at Mach 4 is investigated using Direct Simulation Monte Carlo across Reynolds numbers from 270 to 6750, spanning slip-flow to near-continuum regimes. Power Spectral Density analysis at discrete probe locations and Dynamic Mode Decomposition of flowfield snapshots independently characterize instabilities in both the stagnation and wake regions. In the stagnation region, a bow shock pulsation mode at 10-15 MHz frequency is identified across all cases despite a 24-fold variation in number density. In the wake, two distinct instabilities are observed. The canonical vortex shedding mode at Strouhal number St $\approx$ 0.2 dominates at lower Reynolds numbers. A second instability at St $\approx$ 0.5, consistent with previously reported slipline-driven oscillations in supersonic wakes, emerges at higher Reynolds numbers and progressively strengthens, becoming the dominant mode. In the studied Reynolds range, the wake transitions from no clear unsteadiness, to canonical vortex shedding at St $\approx$ 0.20, and reaching a regime where the St $\approx$ 0.5 mode becomes dominant, while also having a distinct independent bow shock pulsation possibly governed by its standoff distance.
item.dc:creator: Mert Senkardesler, Irmak T. Karpuzcu, Deborah A. Levin

item.title: Magnetic crystal generation with site-resolved magnetic moments via Gaussian-mixture retargeting and finite-budget yield prediction
item.description: arXiv:2610.37222v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce GMMag, a workflow for generating crystal structures together with their site-resolved magnetic moments, built on a conditional variational autoencoder with a graph neural network encoder and a transformer decoder. Gaussian-mixture sampling redirects generation towards selected chemical and magnetic targets without retraining. We systematically investigate how encoder and decoder design, the representation of magnetic-moment magnitudes and relative signs, and sampling choices affect reconstruction, generation quality and diversity. Because a higher screening pass rate does not necessarily yield more qualifying candidates with distinct chemical formulas absent from the reference dataset, we model how repeated generation of the same chemical formulas limits their accumulation and test the model in two separate ten-million-draw runs. As an application, the workflow identifies Nd-containing candidates with chemical formulas absent from the reference dataset, negative formation energies and high estimated saturation magnetization.
item.dc:creator: Wen-Chuang Shang, Chenyu Shen, Mikito Tsujimoto, Tomonori Tanaka, Yoshihiro Gohda

item.title: diff-soup: GPU-native Differentiable Simulation and Inference for Large-scale Stiff Dynamical Systems
item.description: arXiv:2610.37333v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Learning physical models from spatiotemporal data requires simulating systems of partial differential equations (PDEs) and differentiating through their solution. Upon spatial discretization, these models give rise to stiff dynamical systems that require repeatedly solving large, sparse linear systems. Traditional scientific computing frameworks are largely CPU-based and require problem-specific tuning to accelerate, scale, and differentiate. In this work, we introduce diff-soup, a differentiable, sparse-oriented, unified PDE suite for GPU-native simulation and inference of large, stiff dynamical systems. Built in JAX, diff-soup provides 1) a fully differentiable design for problems with sparse structure, 2) scaling to large problems through the NVIDIA cuDSS sparse direct solver with model and data multi-GPU parallelism, and 3) end-to-end PDE-constrained optimization, from classical statistical inference to embedded deep learning. On stiff PDE benchmarks, diff-soup outperforms established CPU- and GPU-based frameworks by one to two orders of magnitude in both forward solves and gradients. We demonstrate both a classical Bayesian inference workflow, identifying constitutive relationships, and a modern deep learning workflow, training a neural field for the catalyst activity of a three-dimensional packed bed reactor. We provide diff-soup as an open-source repository to facilitate research in computational science and engineering.
item.dc:creator: Samuel Degnan-Morgenstern, Martin Z. Bazant

item.title: AMOR: Adaptive Modal Operator Refinement for Operator Learning on Arbitrary Meshes and Irregular 3D Geometries
item.description: arXiv:2610.37485v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Parametric PDEs in science and engineering are often posed on irregular meshes with geometries that may contain holes or complex boundaries, yet popular operator-surrogate architectures such as the Fourier Neural Operator (FNO) rely on structured geometries for fast computational kernels. We introduce Adaptive Modal Operator Refinement (AMOR), which replaces FNO's Fourier-based spectral convolutions with reduced-basis blocks and supports both data-driven and prescribed input/output bases through a common encode/decode interface. AMOR thus applies unmodified to arbitrary meshes and, because its spectral parameterization has no tensor-product dependence on the spatial dimension, it scales favorably to three dimensions, where FNO's spectral weights grow as $m^3$ with the number of spectral modes $m$. We prove that AMOR is a universal approximator of continuous operators. On two-dimensional structured-grid benchmarks, AMOR is competitive with FNO overall and surpasses PCANet: it outperforms FNO on nonlinear diffusion and Helmholtz problems, while a static snapshot basis keeps it from matching FNO's accuracy on the time-dependent Kolmogorov flow problem. On three-dimensional problems it matches or exceeds FNO's accuracy at lower inference cost on linear elastostatics while trailing FNO on a turbulent lid-driven-cavity flow and scales favorably to problems demanding high capacity. On irregular meshes, where FNO is not directly applicable, AMOR reduces the relative $L^2$ error over the FNO extension Geo-FNO by $31\%$ (airfoil) and $42\%$ (elasticity). Finally, AMOR maintains strong performance across three physically distinct, experimentally motivated loading regimes on a topologically nontrivial three-dimensional aircraft-rib mesh, demonstrating its applicability to realistic engineering problems without modification.
item.dc:creator: David Voderholzer, Leonard Vetter, Thomas O'Leary-Roseberry

item.title: New Developments in Diagrammatic Monte Carlo for Interacting Lattice Fermions: Efficient Algorithms and Applications
item.description: arXiv:2610.37505v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This thesis develops diagrammatic methods for thermodynamic and subsystem quantities of interacting lattice fermions, providing reference calculations for quantum simulators and many-body approximations. I formulate an inverse-flavour expansion about a self-consistent Hartree saddle, enumerate non-Gaussian diagrams, and use a discrete Lehmann representation to integrate selected internal vertices analytically. Density results cover 31 state points of the six-flavour Hubbard model on a $70\times70$ lattice at $T/t=0.15$. I generalize combinatorial summation to flavour-dependent propagators and expansion shifts. CoS++ combines partial contractions to obtain connected sums for interaction subsets. A determinant-polynomial sieve evaluates the same sums through local coefficient filters; at ninth order it is 24--25 times faster than the specified CoS baselines in three-flavour dense-random-matrix benchmarks. Thermodynamic applications include a 2048-site honeycomb lattice and a three-flavour square lattice with 1024 sites. For the second Renyi entropy, I derive a fermionic replica path integral and a stable evaluation of its two-time Green functions. The connected-determinant calculation reaches tenth order on a $3\times3$ cluster and ninth order on larger lattices. On $50\times50$ sites at $(U/t,\mu/t,\beta t)=(3,1,8)$, the ninth-order continuation at shift $\alpha=1.3$ gives $S_2/N_s=0.06695$ with propagated Monte Carlo uncertainty $3.0\times10^{-5}$. Comparing two expansion shifts at their respective retained orders gives an endpoint difference of $2.6\times10^{-4}$.
item.dc:creator: Boyuan Shi

item.title: Attention as Lattice Gauge Theory: Relations Interact Only Through Wilson Loops
item.description: arXiv:2610.37656v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Relations compose through the entity they share - Alice is Bob's mother and Bob is Carol's father, so Alice is Carol's grandmother - and the order matters, since a father's mother is not a mother's father; verifying a composed relation means closing the loop. We show that if each entity's coordinate frame may be rotated independently (per-entity frame freedom), three things follow. In the pure-gauge sector, relations that share no cycle cannot interact at all. The only gauge-invariant score of a triangle is a class function of its holonomy $H = T_{ij} T_{jk} T_{ki}$ - a Wilson loop. And the only equivariant update of an edge is $U = \Psi(H)\, T_{ij}$ with $\Psi$ conjugation-equivariant. Edge attention by Wilson loops is therefore not one design among many but the unique form the symmetry permits. Three communities hold pieces of this form: the commuting-operator embeddings of knowledge graphs are its abelian (commuting) sector; AlphaFold's triangle update and the Edge Transformer have its shape - an edge updated through the third vertex - without its constraints; and lattice QCD builds it equivariantly on lattices. We instantiate the equivariant sub-family on general relational graphs as holonomy attention. With no training and composition alone, it infers unobserved $S_4$ relations on sparse graphs at 0.88 with a fifth of the edges corrupted, at or slightly below specialist synchronization algorithms, where every commutative architecture is capped at 0.083; its holonomy score flags corrupted triangles at AUC 0.99 where commuting scores are capped at 0.76 by a second selection rule, and it separates clusters without labels.
item.dc:creator: Aakash Sarkar, Ananya Mukherjee, Motoshige Sato

item.title: Generalized Onsager-Regularized Lattice Boltzmann framework
item.description: arXiv:2602.21242v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This work presents a novel strategy to address Navier-Stokes modelling errors arising on first-nearest neighbour lattice Boltzmann (LB) methods and introduces fully local corrections through Onsager-Regularized (OReg) non-equilibrium populations. The proposed mechanism, which admits partially and completely corrected OReg models, is used to develop representative partially and completely corrected models for the six-moment-constrained guided equilibrium (GEq) representation on the D2Q9 lattice. The former realization only addresses compatibility condition violations and improves the accuracy by two/four orders of magnitude at reference/arbitrary lattice temperatures respectively, while the latter additionally corrects stress tensor modelling errors, resulting in a fully corrected exact model. Numerical benchmarks of the corrected schemes demonstrate improved accuracy and stability in comparison to the Lattice-BGK, regularized, and uncorrected OReg-GEq schemes thus presenting a promising avenue for OReg based thermohydrodynamic extensions.
item.dc:creator: Anirudh Jonnalagadda, Walter Rocchia, Sauro Succi

item.title: sft-wick: A formalism and package for Feynman-diagram expansion and evaluation in stochastic field theories
item.description: arXiv:2606.19480v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: When stochastic field dynamics are cast into a path-integral formulation, perturbation theory becomes systematic but the resulting expansion quickly grows combinatorially large. The setting targeted here includes fields with several components and several dimensions, matrix propagators, tensor-valued couplings, and non-Gaussian driving noise specified by arbitrary n-point cumulants. Wick pairings grow factorially, and component indices must be routed through the tensor-valued vertices. The useful output is not a raw contraction list, but a diagram table: one entry per topology, with multiplicities, coupling sums, signs, and causal constraints resolved. We present sft-wick, an open-source Python package that constructs these diagram tables and computes their integrals numerically. Given an action and an observable, it enumerates topologically distinct Feynman diagrams, derives their algebraic coefficients, and evaluates the resulting diagram integrals from user-supplied response and cumulant functions. The core algorithm enumerates spatial topologies before routing component indices, avoiding contraction-by-contraction Wick expansion. Response-field constraints, including vanishing response-response contractions, the Ito prescription, and the absence of causal response loops, are enforced during enumeration. Predictions are validated against direct Langevin simulations in two worked examples, with Gaussian and with non-Gaussian driving noise, and agree with the simulations within stated error budgets.
item.dc:creator: Zheng Zhang

item.title: A neural accelerated roughness-resolved Discrete Element Method (Rough-DEM) for modeling granular systems
item.description: arXiv:2610.33363v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The Discrete Element Method (DEM) is an indispensable tool for modeling and understanding the basic mechanical behaviors of (dry) granular media, a class of disordered material systems of significant interest to multiple scientific domains from (geo-)physics to (chemical) engineering. At the core of all present DEM frameworks is a phenomenological friction law--commonly chosen to be of the Amontons-Coulomb type--that models the frictional interaction among constituent grains. Here, inspired by research in the tribology community, we present an alternative, fundamentally different framework, termed roughness-resolved DEM (Rough-DEM), in which contact friction is handled in a more physics-based manner. In this framework, instead of using a friction law, we explicitly resolve the surface topography of each grain and let friction emerge from collective frictionless interactions of surface asperities. In essence, we trade phenomenology for physics at the cost of an increased computational demand. To mitigate the cost, we introduce an FE$^2$-like algorithm and a feature-wise linear modulation (FiLM)-based neural network surrogate, both of which are parallelized on GPU to accelerate contact computation. Crucially, using this framework in 2D, we (1) demonstrate the possibility of recovering a two-body-based Amontons-Coulomb-type friction behavior using a \textit{simple} representation of surface topography, and (2) identify many-body-based frictional behaviors--more specifically, the angle of repose values--that \textit{cannot always} be captured by current DEM frameworks under the same level of model complexity. We conclude by discussing future directions for Rough-DEM, as well as exciting new opportunities it could unlock for a wide range of emerging applications, including (designing) suspension rheology and metamaterial mechanics.
item.dc:creator: Xiwei Pan, Liuchi Li

item.title: Re4: Scientific Computing Agent with Rewriting, Resolution, Review and Revision
item.description: arXiv:2508.20729v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated abilities to perform complex tasks in multiple domains, including mathematical and scientific reasoning. In this work, we construct a novel agent framework for solving representative problems in scientific computing. The proposed agent incorporates a "rewriting-resolution-review-revision" logical chain via three reasoning LLMs (the Consultant, Reviewer, and Programmer) in a collaborative and interactive manner. The Consultant module enables knowledge transfer to link problems to professional domain insights, thereby rewriting problem descriptions through text augmentation. The Programmer module generates and executes well-structured code to solve problems. The Reviewer module enables self-debugging and self-refinement through interactive feedback with code runtime outputs. Through the end-to-end review mechanism, the Programmer's executable code undergoes iterative revision. We comprehensively evaluate the framework on typical partial differential equations (PDEs), engineering-oriented flow past a cylinder, ill-conditioned linear systems, and data-driven physical analysis problems. Compared with a single-model approach, this collaborative framework significantly improves the bug-free code generation rate and reduces non-physical solutions, establishing a reliable framework for autonomous code generation from natural language descriptions. The review mechanism improved the average execution success (bug-free code and non-NaN solutions) rate of DeepSeek R1 from 59% to 82%, while ChatGPT 4.1-mini improved from 66% to 87% and Gemini-2.5 improved from 60% to 84%. Automatic code generation and review provide a promising workflow for scientific computing; analysis of solver-development trajectories further reveals recurring implementation difficulties in boundary treatment, array indexing, and the preservation of numerical constraints.
item.dc:creator: Ao Cheng, Lei Zhang, Guowei He

item.title: PhysGuard: Fisher-Guided Gradient Projection for Sim-to-Real Neural PDE Surrogates
item.description: arXiv:2606.16602v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Neural operator models trained on simulation data often lose accuracy when applied to experimental measurements due to the sim-to-real gap. Standard fine-tuning with limited real data can reduce this gap, but it may also damage the core physics-relevant representations learned during pretraining. Although knowledge-preserving adaptation has been widely investigated in vision or language tasks, it remains unclear whether these methods are suitable for neural operators whose architectures and protected knowledge are fundamentally different. Neural operators need to preserve core-scale physical structures rather than semantic or visual features. We propose PhysGuard, a physics-preserving framework for accurate sim-to-real adaptation of neural operators. Specifically, PhysGuard uses the empirical Fisher Information Matrix computed on simulation data to identify physics-critical parameter directions, then restricts fine-tuning updates to directions that do not interfere with them. A layer-wise Gram-matrix formulation makes this efficient for models with millions of parameters, while an adaptive threshold automatically determines the protected subspace size. A spectral probe experiment shows that the dominant Fisher directions are strongly associated with low-frequency output structures. Experiments on benchmark across four neural operator architectures and different physical systems show that PhysGuard performs strongly on most evaluation metrics compared to baselines. The benefits are most evident under severe domain shift, where it reduces low-frequency error by up to 32% compared to standard fine-tuning while maintaining adaptability. Our code is available at https://github.com/Data-Driven-Computational-Geotechnics/PhysGuard.
item.dc:creator: Changjian Zhou, Junfeng Fang, Negin Yousefpour, Peng Wu, Bin Yan, Guillermo A. Narsilio

item.title: EFT-Ramses: a code to simulate the effective field theory of dark energy
item.description: arXiv:2607.24940v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: While the standard $\Lambda$CDM paradigm is in excellent agreement with most current cosmological observations, theoretical challenges surrounding the cosmological constant ($\Lambda$) have strongly motivated the exploration of dynamical dark energy (DE) and modified gravity (MG) models. Investigating the physical nature of the cosmic acceleration requires N-body simulations to probe the non-linear growth of cosmic structure and prepare for the high-precision data from Stage-IV surveys. In this paper, we present EFT-RAMSES, a comprehensive extension of the ECOSMOG cosmological simulation code designed to explore non-linear structure formation in DE and MG scenarios. We embed the effective field theory of dark energy (EFTofDE) framework into this new numerical pipeline, utilising the $\alpha$-basis parameterisation to provide a versatile, model-agnostic, computational engine. By consolidating diverse scalar and vector-tensor theories---including the normal and self-accelerating Dvali-Gabadadze-Porrati (DGP) models, cubic Galileons (cubic scalar Galileon (csG), cubic vector Galileon (cvG) and generalised cubic covariant Galileon (GCCG)), and generic effective field theory (EFT) parameterisation---into a single "master" Vainshtein equation, this pipeline bypasses the need for model-specific solvers and easily specialises to any particular model. As validations, we perform high-resolution N-body simulations for the normal-branch DGP (nDGP), csG, GCCG, and EFT models, comparing the resulting matter power spectra against dependent and independent codes such as legacy ECOSMOG and HiCOLA, as well as linear theory, and find excellent agreement. EFT-RAMSES provides a robust and versatile computational tool for precision cosmological tests of DE and MG using upcoming cosmological surveys. The code is available for download from the GitHub EFT-RAMSES repository.
item.dc:creator: Nathaniel Ota Woodcock, Sownak Bose, Yunhao Gao, Baojiu Li

item.title: Dynamics-aware bandwidth selection for smoothed charge deposition in 2D electrostatic particle-in-cell
item.description: arXiv:2610.03230v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Charge deposition in the particle-in-cell (PIC) method can be viewed as kernel density estimation on a spatial mesh. This allows the smoothing bandwidth to be selected through statistical criteria such as mean integrated squared error or cross-validation, but it also changes the electric field acting on the particles. Therefore, a selected bandwidth can alter the growth or damping of physical modes. We develop a dynamics-aware bandwidth-selection procedure that combines a density-error objective with constraints on specified linear modes. These constraints follow from the plasma equilibrium and the combined transfer of deposition, filtering and field gathering within the model rate-tolerance boundary. We demonstrate the need for equilibrium information through a controlled two-stream experiment. The controlled two-stream scan varies the beam drift while holding the initial spatial density, thermal samples, wavevector and fixed-filter transfer unchanged. Across four resolved equilibria approaching marginal stability, this filter reduces the measured growth rate by $0.7\%$ to $9.1\%$. Equilibrium-dependent interior settings satisfy the prescribed $10\%$ rate tolerance. We then apply the constrained selection rule to 85 Gaussian candidates, that reduces density and grid-field mean-square errors by $7.40\%$ and $3.70\%$ on independently evaluated snapshots. A separate projected-linear calculation at that exact width gives a ratio of mean individual growth rates of $0.9556$, with paired $95\%$ interval $[0.9453,0.9640]$, consistent with the prediction $0.9513$. Analysis of finite-marker loading and ensemble averaging explains how the measured rates relate to the response model. Together, these results demonstrate a filter-design procedure that combines statistical error reduction with subsequent validation of the selected linear dynamics.
item.dc:creator: Ayushi Agrawal, Shan-Chang Lin, Ezhilmathi Krishnasamy, Pascal Bouvry

item.title: Inverse Design of Integrated Photonic Components for Visible-Light Applications
item.description: arXiv:2610.11453v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Photonic integrated circuits (PICs) operating in the visible spectral range are crucial for quantum technologies, optical sensing, and nonlinear optics applications. However, their development is hampered by limited integration density and operational bandwidth, linked to low refractive index contrast and restricted parameter space in intuition-based PIC design. We address these bottlenecks with an adjoint-based, fabrication-aware inverse design workflow tailored for visible-spectrum photonics. By expanding the capabilities of FDTDX, an open-source, GPU-accelerated FDTD solver, we provide a versatile memory and runtime efficient inverse design platform. Demonstrating this approach on a silicon nitride (Si3N4) platform, we design, fabricate, and experimentally validate ultra-compact, broadband components for light routing, multiplexing, and polarization control. This work provides a scalable framework for high-density, high-performance visible-light PICs.
item.dc:creator: Christoph Stockinger, Marko \v{S}imi\'c, John O. Adeniran, Natale G. Pruiti, Marc Sorel, Peter Banzer
